channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: High-Accuracy Neural-Network Quantum States via Randomized Real-Time Dynamics
item.description: Neural-network quantum states (NQSs) exhibit a disparity in converging to the ground state during energy minimization: while the energy converges quadratically with the error in the variational wave function, other observables converge only linearly, which limits the accuracy of physical predictions. Here we show how to close this gap by introducing a new algorithm that improves the accuracy of NQSs.

item.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
item.description: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

item.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model
item.description: Global Workspace Theory (GWT), a leading theory of consciousness, holds that information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialized processes that use it. Building a workspace into a network does not reveal what the trained network computes with it: a module that reports an answer may have combined a broadcast message with its own knowledge, or merely forwarded an answer computed elsewhere, and task accuracy and ablation cannot tell these apart.

item.title: A Quantum Genetic Algorithm for Optimization of Benchmark Test Functions using Entangled Qutrits
item.description: Typically, quantum genetic algorithms are based on qubits, a two-level quantum system. This work investigates the optimization of Rastrigin, Rosen-Brock and Table Holder Function in comparison with Classical Genetic Algorithm (CGA), using two quantum approaches: Quantum Genetic Algorithm (QGA), and Higher-Order Quantum Genetic Algorithm (HO-QGA) based on qutrits, a three-level system.

item.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
item.description: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.

item.title: Multimodal Coma Stimulation to Improve Arousal and Physical Function in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury
item.description: Background: Impaired consciousness is one of the most serious complications following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Sensory deprivation may delay neural recovery and worsen patient outcomes.

item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future e + e − colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes e + e − → t t ‾ , e + e − → μ + μ − and Bhabha scattering e + e − → e + e − , representing the mass threshold behavior, the Z pole resonance and the s / t -channel interplay.

item.title: Nondiagonal Lindblad master equations in quantum reservoir engineering
item.description: Reservoir engineering has proven to be a practical approach to control open quantum systems, preserving quantum coherence by appropriately manipulating the reservoir and system-reservoir interactions. In this context, for systems comprised of different parts, it is common to describe the dynamics of a subsystem of interest by performing an adiabatic elimination of the remaining components of the system.

item.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
item.description: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

item.title: Quantum Entanglement, Consciousness and the Principles of New AI
item.description: Centered on statistical fitting and pattern matching, modern artificial intelligence merely simulates specific tasks. It lacks consistent logical reasoning, creative intuition, genuine emotional valence and moral judgment, stemming from the failure of existing computing frameworks to capture the fundamental physical mechanisms behind quantum entanglement and human consciousness.

item.title: C2 |Q⟩: A Robust Framework for Bridging Classical and Quantum Software Development
item.description: Quantum Software Engineering (QSE) is emerging as a critical discipline to make quantum computing accessible to a broader developer community; however, most quantum development environments still require developers to engage with low-level details across the software stack—including problem encoding, circuit construction, algorithm configuration, hardware selection and result interpretation—making them difficult for classical software engineers to use. item.title: Algorithmic Quantum Sensing
item.description: We introduce a unified framework for sensing time-dependent fields through the lens of classical and quantum algorithms. First, we develop three pulse sequence protocols, namely randomized, matched, and pooled spectroscopy, which outperform established approaches such as dynamical decoupling across a wide range of tasks.

item.title: From AGI to AI Welfare: Computational Functionalism and Its Consequences
item.description: Claims that artificial intelligence has reached or is approaching artificial general intelligence (AGI) are increasingly widespread in both industry and academia. These claims typically rest on either behavioral benchmark tests or mechanistic interpretability findings.

item.title: Performance comparison of QAOA mixers for ternary portfolio optimization
item.description: The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is a quantum algorithm proposed for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices and is regarded as a promising approach to combinatorial optimization problems, with potential applications in the financial sector. In this study, we apply QAOA to the portfolio optimization problem, which is one of the central challenges in financial engineering.

item.title: Scalable Simulation of Strongly Correlated Fermions with Neural Gaussian Tensor Networks
item.description: Accurate simulations of strongly correlated electrons remain a central challenge in computational physics. We introduce neural-network Gaussian projected entangled-pair states (NN-GPEPS), which exploit the locally-entangled subspace of Gaussian states to give an architecture more compatible with modern neural networks and an exact contraction cost of $O(N^{3/2})$ on two-dimensional lattices.

item.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction
item.description: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a classical decoder fast enough to process syndrome measurements at the rate at which they are generated, and to return its decisions with low latency. This is most demanding for superconducting processors, whose fast syndrome cycles force a trade-off between decoding speed and accuracy.
